preamble: Vocalization of a nasal consonant to the vowel [i]. In Spokane (Interior Salish), the process known as nasal shift turns a nasal immediately followed by a coronal fricative (/s/, /š/, also /h/) into the glide [j], or into the vowel [i] when syllabification requires a nucleus. It most often affects the final /n/ of a root or suffix before /s/, and also applies to /m/ (e.g. k'ʷúpiš 'push something!' < √k'ʷup-m-š). It is a morphophonemic rule rather than automatic allophony: it is not fully general, is restricted to certain morphological domains (prefixal and suffixal, not root-internal), and competes with nasal deletion and fricative hardening in the same environment.

examples.note: The root-final /n/ before the possessive suffix -s surfaces as syllabic [i].
The /n/ of the proclitic čn becomes [i] before /s/ within the prefixal domain; compare hin-s-√mʔem > hismʔém 'she is my woman', where the /n/ deletes instead.
Non-syllabic outcome of the same process: the nasal before /s/ surfaces as the glide [j] (Americanist ⟨y⟩).
